acceptance: A test runs `make -n <target>` for every affected target in a temporary repository with a fake gh and a bare remote, and asserts no push, no gh call, no receipt or merge, and the documented exit status.
The PR records an inventory of make/*.mk targets whose recipe line contains $(MAKE) and has external side effects; each is fixed or covered.
context:
Owner decision 2026-11-19: default accepted; reuse the existing MAKEFLAGS dry-run guard convention from make/quality.mk.

2026-11-20 done: #4397 merged (9703d6d9). Landing targets whose recipe line contains $(MAKE) refuse or report under make -n/-q/-t before any side effect, using the existing MAKEFLAGS word-scan convention from make/quality.mk (handles GNU Make 3.81 placing -n after long options; ignores title words and flags with inline arguments). The timing wrapper make_timing_shell.sh skips recording under the same scan. Tests run make -n per affected target in a temp repo with fake gh and a bare remote (no push, no gh call, no receipt or merge). Inventory recorded in the PR body.
description:
GNU make executes any recipe line containing $(MAKE) even under -n, -q or -t. The pr-open recipe in make/pr-landing.mk is one logical line that calls $(MAKE) -s agent-write-preflight, so `make -n pr-open` pushes the branch and opens a PR. Other landing targets whose recipe line contains $(MAKE) also run under -n: pr-preflight (full preflight, writes a receipt), pr-refresh (git merge, then a nested pr-open that also runs), pr-fanout (runs pr-open in every worktree), pr-preflight-fast-tests, pr-content-guard, pr-ready and pr-arm-auto-merge. pr-arm has no $(MAKE) and is safe. The pr-open push was observed during the 0.5.1 release session; no run or PR records it.

Decision gate: default is to reuse the existing dry-run guard (make/quality.mk skill-sync's MAKEFLAGS word loop, and ci-lint) so -n refuses or reports and exits before any side effect. Moving $(MAKE) onto its own line is the alternative. The owner decides only if a target cannot take the guard. No second guard convention.

Guardrails: no separate DRY_RUN path that diverges from the real recipe; no existing refusal weakened; tests touch no network (fake gh, bare local remote).
